media_mentions.content_title: Longitudinal Trajectories of Platelet Indices Across Dengue Severity in Children: A Linear Mixed-Model Analysis
media_mentions.content: Abstract Background Dengue has a high disease burden, and some affected children progress to severe dengue (SD), making early identification of deterioration a clinical priority. Automated platelet indices such as mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), and plateletcrit (PCT) are generated at no additional cost by routine hematology analyzers. However, they are usually interpreted as static measurements and cannot distinguish peripheral platelet destruction from impaired bone marrow production. Linear mixed modeling (LMM) is well suited to correlated repeated measurements but has rarely been applied to platelet-index kinetics in pediatric dengue, particularly to distinguish dengue with warning signs (DWS) from SD. The objective of this study was to compare the longitudinal trajectories of eight automated platelet indices across dengue severity groups in hospitalized children using LMM and to assess whether platelet-index trajectories provide additional information beyond platelet count alone. Methods This prospective observational cohort included 130 children with dengue: 14 with dengue fever (DF), 80 with DWS, and 36 with SD, enrolled at a tertiary referral center. Platelet count, PCT, MPV, PDW, mean platelet component (MPC), mean platelet mass (MPM), large platelet percentage, and the composite platelet index (CPLI) were measured on study days 1, 3, 5, and 7. Study day 1 was the enrolment/admission day, which occurred within five days of fever onset. Separate LMMs were fitted for each index with fixed effects of severity group, illness day, age, sex, and a severity × day interaction, and a patient-level random intercept. Results Five indices were associated with dengue severity. Platelet count (day × severity interaction, p < 0.001), PCT (p < 0.001), large platelet percentage (p = 0.035), and CPLI (p < 0.001) showed significant severity-dependent trajectories. MPC was significantly associated with severity overall (p = 0.004), with a borderline day × severity interaction (p = 0.066). MPC showed progressive decline in SD from 26.1 g/dL (day 1) to 24.4 g/dL (day 5), signalling sustained platelet activation while remaining stable in DF. By day 3, CPLI was the only index with non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals between SD (1.46-3.74) and DWS (3.78-5.27). Large platelet percentage increased from 1.63% to 2.29% in DWS between study days 1 and 3 (absolute increase, 0.66 percentage points), compared with an increase from 1.18% to 1.28% in SD (absolute increase, 0.10 percentage points). This pattern is consistent with preserved compensatory thrombopoiesis in DWS and impaired compensation in SD. An exploratory day-1 profile of low platelet count, low CPLI, and a low large platelet percentage was observed in SD. MPV, PDW, and MPM did not discriminate by severity. Conclusions Platelet count, PCT, large platelet percentage, and CPLI showed severity-associated longitudinal trajectories in hospitalized children with dengue. The SD pattern is consistent with concurrent platelet consumption and impaired compensatory thrombopoiesis. These findings require multicenter validation, analyzer standardization, and formal prognostic evaluation before clinical application. Introduction Dengue virus infection is a major global health burden, causing an estimated 390 million infections annually, predominantly in tropical and subtropical regions, including the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia [1]. Although most pediatric infections are self-limited, some progress to severe dengue (SD), characterized by plasma leakage, hemorrhage, or multi-organ dysfunction and associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and health-system strain [2]. Early identification of children at risk is essential because timely supportive care reduces case fatality [3]. Risk stratification nevertheless continues to rely heavily on warning signs and serial platelet counts, which may lag the underlying pathophysiology and provide insufficient early discrimination [4]. Automated platelet indices, including mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), and plateletcrit (PCT), are generated at no additional procedural cost by routine hematology analyzers and have attracted interest as prognostic markers in dengue [5,6]. These indices have proposed mechanistic relevance, though interpretation requires caution because MPV is influenced by multiple biological and analytical factors and is not itself a direct measure of thrombopoiesis. Elevated MPV may reflect compensatory thrombopoiesis and the release of larger, metabolically active platelets during peripheral immune-mediated destruction, whereas low MPV may indicate viral suppression of megakaryocyte production [5,7]. However, previous studies have yielded inconsistent findings, partly because platelet indices have generally been assessed at single time points. Values vary by illness day, and isolated measurements cannot distinguish peripheral destruction from impaired marrow production, which evolve differently during dengue [6,8]. This limits their clinical utility as severity markers [5,9]. Because accelerated platelet clearance and impaired megakaryocyte output may coexist [4,10], longitudinal assessment across the febrile and critical phases may better characterize the balance between platelet consumption and compensatory production [5,11]. Most previous dengue platelet-index studies have relied on cross-sectional comparisons or repeated-measures analyses conducted at fixed timepoints [6,9], which can inadequately address irregular sampling intervals and within-patient correlation when follow-up is incomplete or unevenly spaced [12,13]. Linear mixed models (LMMs) account for correlated observations, variable follow-up, and individual differences in temporal trajectories [13,14]. However, LMMs have rarely been applied to platelet-index kinetics in pediatric dengue, particularly to distinguish dengue with warning signs (DWS) from SD [9,11,15]. This study examined the longitudinal trajectories of platelet count, PCT, PDW, MPV, mean platelet mass (MPM), mean platelet component (MPC), large platelet percentage, and the composite platelet index (CPLI) across dengue severity groups in hospitalized children, assessed at protocol-definedstudy days 1, 3, 5, and 7 (distinct from illness day, i.e., day from fever onset, which varied at enrollment and is reported separately). Using LMMs, we sought to identify severity-associated kinetic differences, explore indirect evidence for the balance between platelet consumption and compensatory thrombopoiesis as inferred from platelet-index patterns, and determine whether platelet-index trajectories provide information beyond platelet count alone. Materials & Methods Study design and setting This was a prospective observational study conducted at a tertiary pediatric referral center. Consecutive children admitted with suspected dengue infection were screened for eligibility and enrolled after written informed consent from parents or legal guardians. Ethical permission was obtained from the institutional ethics committee (MGM-ECRHS/2023/41; April 27, 2023). Participants Eligible patients were aged <18 years with laboratory-confirmed dengue, defined by non-structural protein 1 antigen (NS1 Ag) positivity or dengue immunoglobulin M (IgM) positivity, and were admitted within five days of fever onset. Immunoglobulin G (IgG) positivity alone was not considered sufficient to confirm acute dengue. Dengue severity was classified at discharge by the attending clinician according to the 2009 WHO criteria. DF was defined as dengue without warning signs, DWS as dengue with any warning sign, and SD as dengue with severe plasma leakage, severe bleeding, or severe organ dysfunction [5]. Because severity was determined at discharge, classification incorporated the patient's entire clinical course after admission; this study, therefore, evaluates platelet-index trajectories in relation to eventual (discharge) severity classification rather than testing whether early platelet indices prospectively predict subsequent SD. Routine clinical care was guided by standard clinical and laboratory assessment; study-specific platelet-index trajectories were not used to classify severity or direct management. Inclusion criteria included patients with age <18 years, laboratory-confirmed dengue (NS1 antigen positivity or dengue IgM positivity), admission within five days of fever onset, and written informed consent obtained from a parent or legal guardian. Exclusion criteria included known pre-existing hematological disorders (e.g., congenital thrombocytopenia, leukemia), concurrent severe bacterial infection (positive sterile-site culture or sepsis requiring parenteral antibiotics), systemic immunosuppressive therapy within 30 days prior to admission, platelet transfusion prior to admission, and dengue IgG positivity alone (without NS1 or IgM confirmation). Sample size Sample size was determined a priori using G*Power version 3.1 (Heinrich-Heine-Universität Düsseldorf, Düsseldorf, Germany) for a repeated-measures within-between interaction analysis of variance (ANOVA) as an approximation of the LMM approach. Based on a partial η2 of 0.052 from published pediatric dengue platelet-index data [9,16], corresponding to a Cohen’s f of 0.234, the calculation assumed three severity groups, four measurements, a within-subject correlation of 0.35, and a non-sphericity correction of ε = 0.5. A minimum sample size of 105 was required for 95% power at a two-sided α of 0.05. Allowing for 15% dropout or incomplete follow-up, the target sample was 130 participants. This calculation approximates the primary LMM: repeated-measures ANOVA assumes a compound-symmetric covariance structure and does not include covariates, whereas the LMMs used a random-intercept covariance structure and adjusted for age and sex, so achieved power for the eight individual models may differ from this a priori estimate. Measurements Peripheral venous blood was collected in ethylene diamine tetraacetic acid tubes on study days 1, 3, 5, and 7. Study day 1 was the enrollment or admission day, occurring within five days of fever onset; subsequent samples were targeted approximately 48 hours apart. The corresponding illness day from fever onset was recorded for each sample. Study day, rather than illness day, was used as the time metric in all LMMs and figures, because it reflected the protocol-defined sampling schedule common to all participants. Samples were processed within two hours using a Siemens ADVIA 2120 analyzer (Siemens Healthineers, Erlangen, Germany) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Samples with analyzer flags indicating platelet clumping or unreliable indices were repeated or excluded, and exclusions were documented. Internal quality control, maintenance, and calibration followed the manufacturer’s schedule. Laboratory personnel were blinded to clinical severity and outcomes. Eight indices were recorded: platelet count (×103/μL), PCT (%), MPV (fL), PDW (%), MPC (g/dL), MPM (pg), large platelet percentage (%), and CPLI, calculated as platelet count expressed in 105/μL multiplied by MPV in fL. Hemoglobin, hematocrit, and white cell count were measured concurrently. Intensive care unit admission, hospital stay, and mortality were extracted by a team member blinded to platelet-index values. Statistical analysis Continuous variables are presented as mean ± standard deviation or median with interquartile range, and categorical variables as number and percentage. Baseline differences among DF, DWS, and SD were assessed using ANOVA or the Kruskal-Wallis test for continuous variables and the chi-squared or Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables. Separate LMMs were fitted for each platelet index. Fixed effects included severity group, with DF as the reference, study day, age, sex, and the severity × day interaction. Study day was modeled as a continuous variable in the primary analysis, and a patient-level random intercept accounted for within-subject correlation. Random slopes for study day were considered but were not retained because they did not improve model fit or failed to converge. Degrees of freedom were estimated using the Satterthwaite approximation. Although study day was modeled as a continuous fixed effect, the day × severity interaction and severity main-effect F tests reported in the results are the omnibus Type III tests from the GAMLj mixed-model ANOVA output; estimated marginal means (EMMs) at study days 1, 3, 5, and 7 represent model-predicted values at those specific days rather than a categorical day effect. Model performance was summarized using marginal and conditional R2 values. Model assumptions were evaluated by inspecting residuals and random effects, with no major violations of normality or homoscedasticity identified. Post-hoc EMMs with 95% confidence intervals were calculated for study days 1, 3, 5, and 7, adjusted to the cohort mean age and sex. Pairwise between-group contrasts at individual time points were interpreted descriptively; when formally tested, p-values were adjusted for multiple comparisons. Statistical significance was set at a two-sided p < 0.05. No family-wise correction was applied because the eight indices were prespecified tests addressing a single overarching research question rather than independent post hoc comparisons; given the number of indices tested, however, the three non-significant indices (MPV, PDW, MPM) and the borderline MPC interaction are interpreted as exploratory rather than confirmatory. Analyses were performed using jamovi version 2.4.1 (The jamovi project, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia) with the GAMLj module. Results Patient characteristics One hundred and thirty patients were enrolled: 14 (10.8%) DF, 80 (61.5%) DWS, and 36 (27.7%) SD. SD patients were significantly younger (5.4 ± 5.5 vs. 9.6 ± 5.2 years in DWS; p = 0.001). ICU admission was near-universal in SD (34, 94.4%) vs. in DWS (2, 2.5%), and in-hospital mortality occurred exclusively in SD (4/36, 11.1%; p = 0.005). Admission platelet count, PCT, and CPLI were lowest in SD, though differences were not statistically significant at day 1 (all p > 0.05; Table 1). Platelet transfusion was administered to 24 of 130 patients (18.5%). No patient in the dengue fever (DF) group required transfusion, whereas six of 80 patients (7.5%) with DWS received a single transfusion, and 18 of 36 patients (50%) with SD received transfusions (11 received one unit and seven received two units). Discriminating indices All eight LMMs converged successfully using 478 of a theoretical maximum of 520 observations. Missing laboratory data were absent at day 1 across all severity groups, remained minimal at day 3 (0 in DF and DWS; 1/36 in SD), and increased thereafter, reaching 1/14 (7%) at day 5 and 8/14 (57%) at day 7 in DF, 3/80 (4%) at day 5 and 19-21/80 (24-26%) at day 7 in DWS, and 3/36 (8%) at day 5 and 6-7/36 (17-19%) at day 7 in SD, primarily reflecting earlier hospital discharge in milder cases. Significant day × severity interactions were observed for platelet count (F = 4.29, p < 0.001), PCT (F = 3.87, p < 0.001), large platelet percentage (F = 2.29, p = 0.035), and CPLI (F = 3.81, p < 0.001). MPC showed a significant overall severity effect (F = 5.65, p = 0.004), with a borderline day × severity interaction (F = 1.99, p = 0.066). MPV, PDW, and MPM did not show statistically significant severity-associated trajectories (all interaction p > 0.05; Table 2). Conditional R2 for these three exploratory indices ranged from 0.495 to 0.586, compared with 0.516-0.677 for the five severity-associated indices. Longitudinal trajectories of platelet count, large platelet percentage, MPC, and MPV are shown in Figure 1. Severity-stratified trajectories and exploratory day 1 patterns EMMs for the five severity-associated indices are presented in Table 3. At study day 1, EMM platelet count and PCT were approximately 30% lower in SD than in DWS. Between study days 1 and 3, the EMM platelet count decreased from 40.8 to 34.6 ×103/μL in SD (absolute change, -6.2 × 103/μL) and from 59.0 to 57.1 × 103/μL in DWS (absolute change, -1.9 × 103/μL). PCT was essentially unchanged in SD after rounding (0.029% to 0.029%) and increased from 0.043% to 0.046% in DWS. By day 5, platelet count remained approximately 40% lower in SD than DWS (50.8 vs. 84.7 × 103/μL), a gap that persisted to day 7, when SD values remained suppressed relative to DWS (platelet count 85.4 × 103/μL vs 146.7 × 103/μL). The most striking divergence was in thrombopoietic compensation. Large platelet percentage increased from 1.63% to 2.29% in DWS between study days 1 and 3 (absolute increase, 0.66 percentage points), eventually exceeding DF by day 7, whereas SD increased from 1.18% to 1.28% (absolute increase, 0.10 percentage points) despite worse thrombocytopenia. This pattern is consistent with relatively preserved compensatory thrombopoiesis in DWS and impaired compensation in SD. CPLI decreased from 2.93 to 2.60 in SD and increased from 4.27 to 4.52 in DWS over the same interval. At study day 3, the EMM CPLI was 2.60 (95% CI, 1.46-3.74) in SD and 4.52 (95% CI, 3.78-5.27) in DWS. The confidence intervals did not overlap, suggesting separation between these groups at this time point; however, this non-overlap should be interpreted descriptively rather than as a formal test of between-group significance. The EMM MPC in SD decreased from 26.1 g/dL on study day 1 to 24.4g/dL on study day 5, whereas estimates remained relatively stable in DF. Because the day × severity interaction for MPC was borderline, this pattern should be interpreted as a severity-associated trend rather than definitive evidence of a divergent trajectory. papers.abstract: INTRODUÇÃO: As arboviroses são doenças infecciosas relevantes em regiões tropicais e subtropicais, favorecidas pelo clima quente e úmido que contribui para a proliferação de vetores, especialmente mosquitos do gênero Aedes. No Brasil, destacam-se os vírus da dengue (DENV), chikungunya (CHIKV), Zika (ZIKV) e oropouche (OROV), com aumento expressivo de casos e expansão geográfica. Em 2025, foram notificados 1.657.377 casos prováveis de dengue, 4.153 de Zika, 129.480 de chikungunya e 11.987 de Oropouche (BRASIL, 2025), evidenciando a relevância dessas doenças como problema de saúde pública. OBJETIVOS: Realizar vigilância clínica e molecular de casos suspeitos de arboviroses em uma unidade de pronto atendimento em Salvador, Bahia, analisando a circulação viral e sua relação com fatores clínicos e sociodemográficos. METODOLOGIA: Estudo transversal, realizado entre abril de 2023 e março de 2025, na UPA Santo Antônio, Salvador-BA. Incluíram-se indivíduos com sintomas compatíveis com arboviroses, mediante consentimento. Foram coletados dados sociodemográficos, clínicos e amostras de soro, analisadas por ELISA e RT-PCR. RESULTADOS: Foram incluídos 370 participantes, com maior incidência no primeiro semestre dos anos. Quanto à raça/cor, 38,8% se autodeclararam negros, 48,7% pardos e 13,0% brancos. Os sintomas mais frequentes foram febres (97,4%), cefaleia (94,1%), mialgia (89,4%) e artralgia (81,5%). Das 345 amostras testadas, 120 (34,8%) foram positivas. Dengue foi a mais prevalente (23%), seguida por chikungunya (10,7%). O ZIKV apresentou baixa detecção (1,4%). O OROV foi identificado em 3,4% das amostras por RT-PCR. DISCUSSÃO: A detecção de OROV fora da região Amazônica reforça sua expansão geográfica e possível adaptação a vetores urbanos. A co-circulação de arbovírus dificulta o diagnóstico clínico e exige maior sensibilidade da vigilância laboratorial. Fatores ambientais, como chuvas e urbanização, contribuem para a manutenção da transmissão. CONCLUSÃO: Os achados destacam a importância da vigilância integrada para detecção precoce e monitoramento das arboviroses, subsidiando estratégias de controle e políticas públicas voltadas a populações vulneráveis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the growing public health concern of arboviral diseases in tropical and subtropical regions, particularly focusing on the co-circulation of Dengue and Chikungunya viruses and the emergence of Oropouche virus in urban settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted between April 2023 and March 2025 in the UPA Santo Antônio emergency care unit in Salvador, Bahia, involving individuals with symptoms compatible with arboviral diseases who provided consent.
analysis.methods: Sociodemographic, clinical data, and serum samples were collected from participants and analyzed using ELISA and RT-PCR techniques.
analysis.main_results: Out of 370 participants, 345 samples were tested, with 120 (34.8%) being positive for arboviruses. Dengue was the most prevalent (23%), followed by Chikungunya (10.7%), while Oropouche virus was detected in 3.4% of the samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the co-circulation of Dengue and Chikungunya viruses, emphasizing the need for enhanced laboratory surveillance due to the challenges in clinical diagnosis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the importance of integrated surveillance systems for early detection and monitoring of Dengue and other arboviruses, supporting targeted control strategies for vulnerable populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the potential for underreporting due to the reliance on clinical symptoms for case inclusion, but the evidence is strong given the direct molecular testing of samples.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a cross-sectional surveillance of arboviral diseases in an emergency care unit in Salvador, Bahia, between April 2023 and March 2025. It focused on Dengue and Chikungunya viruses, with Oropouche virus also detected. The research aimed to understand the circulation of these viruses and their association with clinical and sociodemographic factors. Out of 370 participants, 345 samples were tested, revealing Dengue as the most prevalent (23%), followed by Chikungunya (10.7%), and Oropouche virus in 3.4% of cases. The study highlights the co-circulation of Dengue and Chikungunya, reinforcing the need for improved laboratory surveillance in urban areas. The findings suggest that environmental factors like rainfall and urbanization contribute to the persistence of these viruses. The study's limitations include its cross-sectional design and potential underreporting based on clinical symptoms, but the evidence is robust due to molecular testing. These results inform the importance of integrated surveillance for early detection and monitoring of Dengue and other arboviruses, supporting targeted public health strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决热带和亚热带地区虫媒病毒性疾病日益引起的公共卫生问题,特别关注登革热和基孔肯雅病毒的共同传播以及奥罗普切病毒在城市环境中的出现。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023 年 4 月至 2025 年 3 月期间,在巴伊亚州萨尔瓦多的 UPA Santo Antônio 急救中心进行了一项横断面研究,研究对象是具有与虫媒病毒性疾病相符症状且已同意的个人。
elements_zh.methods: 从参与者那里收集社会人口学、临床数据和血清样本,并使用 ELISA 和 RT-PCR 技术进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 370 名参与者中,对 345 份样本进行了检测,其中 120 份(34.8%)虫媒病毒呈阳性。登革热最为流行(23%),其次是基孔肯雅热(10.7%),而奥罗普切病毒在 3.4% 的样本中检测到。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了登革热和基孔肯雅病毒的共同传播,并强调由于临床 监测 的挑战,需要加强实验室 监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了综合 监测 系统对于早期检测和监测登革热和其他虫媒病毒的重要性,支持针对弱势群体的有针对性的控制策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横断面设计的限制,并且由于依赖临床症状纳入病例而可能存在漏报的情况,但考虑到对样本的直接分子检测,证据是强有力的。

papers.title: A dengue sob uma perspectiva epidemiológica e sociodemográfica: uma análise sobre o estado de Minas Gerais
papers.abstract: O contexto epidemiológico da dengue no Brasil caracteriza-se por oscilações entre períodos endêmicos e surtos epidêmicos, representando um desafio contínuo à saúde pública. Este estudo tem como objetivo geral analisar o perfil epidemiológico e sociodemográfico da dengue no estado de Minas Gerais, com ênfase no município de Uberlândia, a partir de evidências da literatura científica recente. Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de caráter descritivo e exploratório, realizada em bases de dados nacionais e internacionais. Os resultados indicam elevada incidência da doença em determinados períodos do ano, forte associação com fatores socioambientais, desigualdades regionais e impacto significativo sobre o Sistema Único de Saúde. Conclui-se que a dengue permanece como um importante problema de saúde pública em Minas Gerais, exigindo estratégias integradas de vigilância epidemiológica, controle vetorial e ações intersetoriais.

papers.title: Internists facing emerging arboviral diseases: time to get prepared.
papers.abstract: Abstract Arboviral diseases are emerging and affect approximately 60 million individuals yearly. Climate change, vector migration patterns, urbanisation and global travel are boosting their spread beyond traditionally endemic regions, including Europe. This narrative review provides a practical and clinically oriented overview of the main arthropod-borne viral infections. We summarize their epidemiology, virological features, and transmission, highlighting shared as well as distinctive clinical presentations, diagnostic approaches and current management strategies. Although most infections are asymptomatic or self-limiting, severe complications may occur, including dengue haemorrhagic manifestations and shock, West Nile neuroinvasive disease, congenital and neurological complications of Zika, and chronic disabling arthritis after Chikungunya virus infection. Diagnosis remains challenging due to often nonspecific presentations, and laboratory interpretation may be complicated by timing of sampling and serological cross-reactivity. Since specific antiviral therapies remain largely unavailable, early clinical suspicion, appropriate laboratory testing, supportive care, vaccination (where applicable) and vector-control measures are central to patient management and public health response. Internists frequently evaluate patients with undifferentiated febrile illness in emergency departments and internal medicine units, and play a key role in the correct management of these infections, guiding differential diagnosis, identifying severe presentations, and supporting surveillance and prevention efforts in an era of expanding arboviral risk.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on dengue virus and its associated diseases, including dengue fever, dengue hemorrhagic fever, dengue shock syndrome, and severe dengue. The central question is how internists can prepare for and manage emerging arboviral diseases, particularly those caused by dengue viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature on dengue viruses and related arboviruses. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods. The review includes general background and methods information, but no explicit details on study design or population selection.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that dengue viruses 1–4 cause dengue disease, which can range from asymptomatic to severe forms such as dengue hemorrhagic fever and dengue shock syndrome. It also notes that other flaviviruses like Zika, West Nile, and yellow fever are biologically related but not the primary focus of this review.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies challenges in diagnosing dengue infections due to nonspecific clinical presentations and potential serological cross-reactivity. It also notes that specific antiviral therapies are not yet available, leaving supportive care and vector control as critical management strategies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for early clinical suspicion, appropriate laboratory testing, and supportive care in managing dengue infections. It also highlights the importance of internists in guiding differential diagnosis, identifying severe cases, and supporting surveillance and prevention efforts.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses the growing threat of dengue virus and its associated diseases, such as dengue fever, dengue hemorrhagic fever, and dengue shock syndrome. It outlines the impact of climate change, vector migration, and urbanization on the spread of dengue beyond traditional endemic regions. The review underscores the challenges in diagnosing dengue due to nonspecific symptoms and serological cross-reactivity, and highlights the lack of specific antiviral therapies. It stresses the role of internists in managing these infections through early suspicion, laboratory testing, and supportive care, while also advocating for improved surveillance and prevention strategies. The review serves as a call to action for healthcare professionals to be prepared for the increasing burden of dengue in a changing global environment.

papers.title: Eco-safe citral nanoemulsion for Aedes albopictus control: Mechanistic multi-target toxicological evaluation integrating molecular docking.
papers.abstract: The widespread transmission of mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and yellow fever by Aedes albopictus necessitates environmentally sustainable vector control solutions. This study developed and characterized a citral-based nanoemulsion using Tween 80 via low-energy emulsification, aiming to enhance larvicidal efficacy and environmental safety. Larvicidal bioassays against third instar A. albopictus revealed significantly higher potency for citral nanoemulsion (LC 50 : 18.886 mg/L; LC 90 : 78.209 mg/L) compared to unformulated citral (LC 50 : 25.777 mg/L; LC 90 : 99.481 mg/L). Morphological study and SEM analysis demonstrated severe structural damage in nanoemulsion-treated larvae, including cuticle collapse, spiracle deformation, and anal gill disfigurement. Biochemical assays indicated elevated catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, suggesting oxidative stress induction. Molecular docking revealed moderate to high binding affinities of citral to CAT (-6.3 kcal/mol), SOD (-4.5 kcal/mol), acetylcholine receptor (AChR; -6.0 kcal/mol), and juvenile hormone-binding protein (JHBP; -7.0 kcal/mol), involving hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. These interactions imply multi-target disruption of antioxidant defence, neural signalling, and endocrine regulation, contributing to larval mortality. Environmental safety evaluation using Chironomus larvae showed low acute toxicity (<10% immobilization at 52.136 mg/L), indicating selective action toward target species. Collectively, the findings highlight citral nanoemulsion as a potent, biodegradable and target-specific larvicide with minimal non-target effects, aligning with sustainable mosquito control strategies. Future work should focus on field validation, adult mosquito susceptibility, and chronic ecological safety to facilitate large-scale application.

papers.title_zh: 用于控制白纹伊蚊的环保柠檬醛纳米乳剂:整合分子对接的多靶点毒理学评估机制
papers.source_body_en: The widespread transmission of mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and yellow fever by Aedes albopictus necessitates environmentally sustainable vector control solutions. This study developed and characterized a citral-based nanoemulsion using Tween 80 via low-energy emulsification, aiming to enhance larvicidal efficacy and environmental safety. Larvicidal bioassays against third instar A. albopictus revealed significantly higher potency for citral nanoemulsion (LC 50 : 18.886 mg/L; LC 90 : 78.209 mg/L) compared to unformulated citral (LC 50 : 25.777 mg/L; LC 90 : 99.481 mg/L). Morphological study and SEM analysis demonstrated severe structural damage in nanoemulsion-treated larvae, including cuticle collapse, spiracle deformation, and anal gill disfigurement. Biochemical assays indicated elevated catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, suggesting oxidative stress induction. Molecular docking revealed moderate to high binding affinities of citral to CAT (-6.3 kcal/mol), SOD (-4.5 kcal/mol), acetylcholine receptor (AChR; -6.0 kcal/mol), and juvenile hormone-binding protein (JHBP; -7.0 kcal/mol), involving hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. These interactions imply multi-target disruption of antioxidant defence, neural signalling, and endocrine regulation, contributing to larval mortality. Environmental safety evaluation using Chironomus larvae showed low acute toxicity (<10% immobilization at 52.136 mg/L), indicating selective action toward target species. Collectively, the findings highlight citral nanoemulsion as a potent, biodegradable and target-specific larvicide with minimal non-target effects, aligning with sustainable mosquito control strategies. Future work should focus on field validation, adult mosquito susceptibility, and chronic ecological safety to facilitate large-scale application.

papers.title: How host mobility formulations shape estimates of pathogen dispersal and epidemic risk in non endemic regions.
papers.abstract: The global warming effects of climate change favor the stable residence of invasive vectors, such as the mosquito Aedes albopictus, in temperate areas, like the Mediterranean basin or north America. Thus, favorable weather conditions, together with human mobility, increase the likelihood of large-scale vector-borne disease epidemics in areas where they were historically not endemic. While mathematical modeling acknowledges the relevance of human mobility in the persistence or prevalence of vector-borne diseases in endemic areas, the combined role of host-mediated vector transport and long-range airline travel in the emergence of epidemics in non-endemic areas is poorly understood. In this context, the impact of specific modeling formulations of human mobility on the epidemic predictions remains elusive. To bridge this gap, we compare two alternative models - one based on the force of infection from different source locations and one based on the explicit physical diffusion of individuals - that incorporate intra- and inter-country human mobility (considering air traffic flows), vector dispersal, and human-mediated vector mobility (e.g., vectors in cars/trains), with applications to diseases such as chikungunya, dengue and Zika. Through extensive computational and analytical analysis, we assess how implicit assumptions and the inclusion of different mobility components influence model estimates of epidemic emergence risk, the timing of potential epidemics and the risk of epidemic spread. The comparison between the two frameworks is illustrated using synthetic networks and Italy as a realistic case study. Our findings show that different model formulations of human mobility yield divergent risk assessment, affecting predictions of large scale outbreaks and importation times driven by explained mechanistic difference. Despite these differences, both models show consistent qualitative patterns in the spatial risk and the likelihood of concurrent local outbreaks. Integrating multiple mobility components and carefully identifying assumptions that reflect observed mechanisms are essential for understanding epidemics in currently non-endemic areas.

While mathematical modeling acknowledges the relevance of human mobility in the persistence or prevalence of vector-borne diseases in endemic areas, the combined role of host-mediated vector transport and long-range airline travel in the emergence of epidemics in non-endemic areas is poorly understood. In this context, the impact of specific modeling formulations of human mobility on the epidemic predictions remains elusive. To bridge this gap, we compare two alternative models - one based on the force of infection from different source locations and one based on the explicit physical diffusion of individuals - that incorporate intra- and inter-country human mobility (considering air traffic flows), vector dispersal, and human-mediated vector mobility (e.g., vectors in cars/trains), with applications to diseases such as chikungunya, dengue and Zika. Through extensive computational and analytical analysis, we assess how implicit assumptions and the inclusion of different mobility components influence model estimates of epidemic emergence risk, the timing of potential epidemics and the risk of epidemic spread. The comparison between the two frameworks is illustrated using synthetic networks and Italy as a realistic case study. Our findings show that different model formulations of human mobility yield divergent risk assessment, affecting predictions of large scale outbreaks and importation times driven by explained mechanistic difference. Despite these differences, both models show consistent qualitative patterns in the spatial risk and the likelihood of concurrent local outbreaks. Integrating multiple mobility components and carefully identifying assumptions that reflect observed mechanisms are essential for understanding epidemics in currently non-endemic areas.

The findings are based on computational analysis and synthetic networks, which provide moderate confidence in the conclusions.

papers.abstract_zh: 气候变化引发的全球变暖效应有利于入侵性媒介(如白纹伊蚊Aedes albopictus)在温带地区(如地中海盆地或北美)的稳定定殖。因此,有利的天气条件与人类流动性共同增加了在历史上非流行区发生大规模媒介媒介传染病流行的可能性。虽然数学建模已认识到人类流动性在流行区患病率持续或复发中的重要性,但宿主介导的媒介传播与长途航空旅行在非流行区流行暴发中的联合作用尚未得到充分理解。在此背景下,特定人类流动性建模形式对流行预测的影响仍有待阐明。为弥补这一缺口,本研究比较了两种替代模型——一种基于不同源地点传染力的模型,另一种基于个体显式物理扩散的模型——这些模型均整合了区内与跨国人类流动性(考虑航空客流)、媒介扩散及人类介导的媒介移动性(如通过汽车/火车携带媒介),并应用于登革热、基孔肯雅热与寨卡病等疾病。通过大规模计算与解析分析,本研究评估了隐含假设及不同流动性组分的纳入如何影响流行暴发风险、潜在流行发生时间及流行扩散风险的模型估计。两种框架的比较通过合成网络与意大利这一现实案例研究进行说明。研究结果显示,不同的人类流动性模型形式会产生分歧的风险评估,影响对大规模暴发与输入时间的预测,其差异可通过解释性机制差异得到说明。尽管如此,两种模型在空间风险与同时发生的局部暴发可能性方面仍显示出一致的定性模式。整合多种流动性组分并谨慎识别反映观察机制的假设,对于理解当前非流行区的流行动态至关重要。

papers.title: Local Linear Estimation for Covariate-Dependent Coefficients Model in Disease Mapping.
papers.abstract: Spatial regression effects may depend on covariates in disease-mapping models. For example, the association between infectious disease incidence and risk factors may vary according to climatic factors, such as time, season, and temperature. In this study, we aim to develop a spatial model that accounts simultaneously for the spatial and varying effects of covariates believed to modulate the spatial association. We employ a local linear estimation method to estimate covariate-dependent coefficients in a model for excess zero counts. The local linear estimator effectively smooths covariate-dependent coefficient estimation. Comprehensive simulation studies were conducted to evaluate the performance of the local linear estimators, and reported dengue cases in villages in Kaohsiung City from January 2014 to December 2015 are used to inform our proposed method for practical use in real-world applications.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for spatial disease-mapping models that can incorporate covariate-dependent effects, noting that associations between infectious disease incidence and risk factors may vary with climatic factors such as time, season, and temperature.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors developed a spatial model to account for spatial and covariate-dependent effects using a local linear estimation method for excess zero counts, with practical application demonstrated using reported dengue cases in villages in Kaohsiung City from January 2014 to December 2015.
analysis.methods: A local linear estimation method was employed to estimate covariate-dependent coefficients in a spatial regression model for excess zero counts, with the approach designed to smooth coefficient estimation.
analysis.main_results: The study conducted comprehensive simulation studies to evaluate the performance of the local linear estimators and applied the method to dengue case data from Kaohsiung City villages during 2014–2015.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the local linear estimator as effectively smoothing covariate-dependent coefficient estimation, highlighting its utility for disease mapping in the presence of covariate effects.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The proposed method may improve spatial disease mapping by accounting for covariate-dependent associations, potentially enhancing surveillance and risk assessment for infectious diseases such as dengue.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level reporting and simulation-based evaluation, with no reported validation in external datasets or clinical outcomes, warranting a low confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a spatial disease-mapping model that incorporates covariate-dependent effects using local linear estimation to address varying associations between risk factors and infectious disease incidence, such as those influenced by climatic factors. The method was applied to dengue case data from Kaohsiung City villages (2014–2015) and evaluated via simulation studies. The local linear estimator is interpreted as effectively smoothing coefficient estimation, offering a potential tool for improving surveillance and risk assessment. However, the evidence is confined to abstract-level descriptions and simulations, lacking external validation or clinical outcome data, which limits confidence in its real-world applicability.

papers.title: Ethical Decision-Making Under Uncertainty in Vector-Borne Zoonotic Disease Control: A One Health Governance Framework
papers.abstract: Decisions about vector-borne zoonotic disease control often have to be made before the evidence is complete. Human surveillance, entomological observations, animal reservoir or sentinel data, environmental indicators, and modelling outputs may provide warning before human disease patterns are clear. In some settings, early action can prevent harm, yet it can also impose social, economic, ecological, animal-welfare, liberty-related, and trust-related burdens. Technical risk assessment remains necessary, although it may need to be complemented by ethical analysis. In this conceptual manuscript, we propose a seven-step One Health ethical decision-making framework that links integrated evidence and transmission plausibility to precaution, proportionality, equity, One Health trade-offs, legitimacy, feedback, impact evaluation, and adaptation. Its contribution lies not in introducing new ethical principles, but in integrating them into an iterative governance sequence and proposing medical bioethics mediation for persistent value conflict. Illustrative domains include West Nile virus, dengue, Zika, Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever, and other mosquito-, tick-, and sand fly-borne zoonotic threats.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Decisions about vector-borne zoonotic disease control often have to be made before the evidence is complete. The study addresses the need for ethical frameworks in managing diseases like dengue where early action is critical but carries significant burdens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a conceptual manuscript proposing a seven-step One Health ethical decision-making framework. It includes illustrative domains such as dengue virus, dengue infection, and related manifestations like severe dengue and dengue hemorrhagic fever.
analysis.methods: The framework integrates evidence from human surveillance, entomological observations, animal reservoir or sentinel data, environmental indicators, and modelling outputs. It emphasizes the necessity of technical risk assessment alongside ethical analysis.
analysis.main_results: The framework outlines a sequence that links integrated evidence and transmission plausibility to precaution, proportionality, equity, One Health trade-offs, legitimacy, feedback, impact evaluation, and adaptation. It does not present new ethical principles but integrates them into a governance process.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as a contribution to ethical decision-making in disease control, emphasizing the integration of ethical principles into a structured governance sequence. The novelty lies in proposing medical bioethics mediation for persistent value conflicts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and control strategies for dengue virus by highlighting the importance of ethical considerations in decision-making processes. They also suggest the need for integrated approaches in managing vector-borne zoonotic diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is conceptual and does not present empirical results, which limits its ability to provide direct evidence on the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The evidence strength is moderate as it is based on theoretical integration rather than practical application.

analysis.summary_en: This conceptual study proposes a seven-step One Health ethical decision-making framework for managing vector-borne zoonotic diseases like dengue. It emphasizes the need for integrating ethical principles with technical risk assessments to guide early interventions. The framework addresses precaution, proportionality, equity, and other governance aspects, aiming to resolve persistent value conflicts through medical bioethics mediation. While the study does not present empirical results, it highlights the importance of ethical considerations in disease control. The findings suggest that such frameworks can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and control strategies for dengue and similar diseases. However, the lack of practical application limits the confidence in its effectiveness, and the evidence strength is considered moderate.

elements_zh.main_results: 该框架概述了一个序列,将综合证据与传播合理性与预防原则、比例原则、公平性、一体化健康权衡、合法性、反馈、影响评估及适应性相联系。它并未提出新的伦理原则,而是将这些原则整合到治理流程中。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为监测、诊断及登革病毒的预防与控制策略提供信息,强调决策流程中伦理考量的重要性。同时,研究还表明在管理媒介传播的人兽共患病时,需要采用综合性方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究为概念性研究,未提供实证结果,因此在评估所提框架有效性方面存在局限。证据强度为中等,因其基于理论整合而非实际应用。

papers.title: Etiological Spectrum of Acute Febrile Illness in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Assam, India: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Introduction: Acute Febrile Illness (AFI) encompasses a spectrum of conditions marked by fever, often caused by various infectious agents. The aetiological diversity poses challenges in diagnosis and treatment, particularly in regions with limited diagnostic resources. Aim: To evaluate the spectrum of pathogens causing AFI with or without rash in patients. Materials and Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2024 to December 2024 on 1,544 patients who had attended Lakhimpur Medical College and Hospital, North Lakhimpur, Assam, India. Patients with fever (≥ 37.5°C) with or without rash were enrolled. Serological investigations for Measles, Rubella, Dengue, Varicella-zoster, Chikungunya viruses, Japanese Encephalitis (JE), Orientia tsutsugamushi, Leptospira, and Hepatitis viruses were performed using Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Rapid Detection Testing (RDT) kits. Data analysis was performed using both descriptive and inferential methods. A p-value of <0.05 was considered significant. Results: Fever was prevalent in all 1,544 (100%) cases, followed by 856 (55.44%) cases of headache, 636 (41.19%) with cough, 476 (30.83%) with vomiting, 347 (22.47%) with abdominal pain, 59 (3.82%) cases with dysentery, 52 (3.37%) with diarrhoea, 46 (2.98%) cases with unconsciousness, and 21 (1.36%) cases presented with rash. Fever was observed in combination with headache in 856 (55.44%), with cough in 636 (41.19%), with bodyache in 481 (31.15%), and with vomiting in 476 (30.83%) cases. The study identified seasonal variations in infection rates, with peaks during the monsoon months. The majority of positive cases were attributed to Scrub Typhus 133/817 (16.28%), followed by Leptospirosis 129/473 (27.27%), Dengue 84/1273 (6.59%), and JE 20/87 (22.99%), while some had co-infection. Conclusion: The study underscores the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches in diagnosing AFI. Scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and dengue were identified as major causes, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Acute Febrile Illness (AFI) encompasses a spectrum of conditions marked by fever, often caused by various infectious agents. The aetiological diversity poses challenges in diagnosis and treatment, particularly in regions with limited diagnostic resources.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2024 to December 2024 on 1,544 patients who had attended Lakhimpur Medical College and Hospital, North Lakhimpur, Assam, India. Patients with fever (≥ 37.5°C) with or without rash were enrolled.
analysis.methods: Serological investigations for Measles, Rubella, Dengue, Varicella-zoster, Chikungunya viruses, Japanese Encephalitis (JE), Orientia tsutsugamushi, Leptospira, and Hepatitis viruses were performed using Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Rapid Detection Testing (RDT) kits. analysis.main_results: The study identified seasonal variations in infection rates, with peaks during the monsoon months. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study underscores the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches in diagnosing AFI. Scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and dengue were identified as major causes, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the necessity for improved diagnostic tools and surveillance systems to address the diverse aetiology of AFI, particularly in resource-limited settings. The seasonal variation in infection rates can inform public health strategies for outbreak prediction and resource allocation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality or temporal relationships. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single hospital's data and does not account for broader population trends.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study conducted in a tertiary care hospital in Assam, India, aimed to evaluate the spectrum of pathogens causing Acute Febrile Illness (AFI) with or without rash. The study included 1,544 patients with fever (≥ 37.5°C) and identified Dengue as one of the major causes, with 84/1273 (6.59%) positive cases. Seasonal variations in infection rates were noted, with peaks during the monsoon months. The results emphasize the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches for accurate diagnosis and highlight the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities. However, the study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate due to its focus on a single hospital's data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 急性发热疾病(AFI)包括一系列以发热为特征的疾病,通常由多种病原体引起。病原体的多样性给诊断和治疗带来了挑战,尤其是在诊断资源有限的地区。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项基于医院的横断面研究,于2024年1月至12月期间在印度阿萨姆邦北拉基姆普尔的拉基姆普尔医学系和医院进行,共纳入1,544名患者。所有发热(≥37.5°C)伴有或不伴有皮疹的患者均被纳入研究。
elements_zh.methods: 对麻疹、风疹、登革热、水痘-带状疱疹病毒、基孔肯雅病毒、日本脑炎(JE)、恙虫病东方体、钩端螺旋体和肝炎病毒进行了血清学检测,使用酶联免疫吸附测定(ELISA)和快速检测测试(RDT)试剂盒。数据采用描述性与推断性统计方法进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究发现感染率存在季节性变化,高峰出现在季风月份。多数阳性病例归因于:丛林斑疹伤寒 133/817(16.28%)、钩端螺旋体病 129/473(27.27%)、登革热 84/1273(6.59%)及日本脑炎 20/87(22.99%),部分病例为混合感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究强调了在诊断AFI时整合临床与实验室方法的重要性。恙虫病、钩端螺旋体病和登革热被确定为主要病因,突显了提升监测和诊断能力的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果突显了在资源有限地区改善诊断工具和监测系统的必要性,以应对AFI的多样化病原体。感染率的季节性变化可为暴发预测和资源分配提供公共卫生策略依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于横断面设计,无法建立因果关系或时间关系。由于基于单一医院的数据,且未考虑更广泛的人群趋势,证据强度中等。

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study underscores the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches in diagnosing AFI. Scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and dengue were identified as major causes, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.

papers.title_zh: 印度阿萨姆邦一所三级医院急性发热疾病的病原谱:一项横断面研究
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Acute Febrile Illness (AFI) encompasses a spectrum of conditions marked by fever, often caused by various infectious agents. The aetiological diversity poses challenges in diagnosis and treatment, particularly in regions with limited diagnostic resources. Aim: To evaluate the spectrum of pathogens causing AFI with or without rash in patients. Materials and Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2024 to December 2024 on 1,544 patients who had attended Lakhimpur Medical College and Hospital, North Lakhimpur, Assam, India. Patients with fever (≥ 37.5°C) with or without rash were enrolled. Serological investigations for Measles, Rubella, Dengue, Varicella-zoster, Chikungunya viruses, Japanese Encephalitis (JE), Orientia tsutsugamushi, Leptospira, and Hepatitis viruses were performed using Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Rapid Detection Testing (RDT) kits. Data analysis was performed using both descriptive and inferential methods. A p-value of <0.05 was considered significant. Results: Fever was prevalent in all 1,544 (100%) cases, followed by 856 (55.44%) cases of headache, 636 (41.19%) with cough, 476 (30.83%) with vomiting, 347 (22.47%) with abdominal pain, 59 (3.82%) cases with dysentery, 52 (3.37%) with diarrhoea, 46 (2.98%) cases with unconsciousness, and 21 (1.36%) cases presented with rash. Fever was observed in combination with headache in 856 (55.44%), with cough in 636 (41.19%), with bodyache in 481 (31.15%), and with vomiting in 476 (30.83%) cases. The study identified seasonal variations in infection rates, with peaks during the monsoon months. The majority of positive cases were attributed to Scrub Typhus 133/817 (16.28%), followed by Leptospirosis 129/473 (27.27%), Dengue 84/1273 (6.59%), and JE 20/87 (22.99%), while some had co-infection. Conclusion: The study underscores the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches in diagnosing AFI. Scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and dengue were identified as major causes, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言:急性发热疾病(AFI)是一组以发热为特征的疾病谱系,常由多种感染性病原体引起。病原学多样性在 诊断 和 治疗 中构成挑战,尤其在诊断资源有限的地区。目的:评估导致伴或不伴皮疹急性发热疾病患者的病原谱。材料与方法:2024年1月至2024年12月,在印度阿萨姆邦北拉金普尔的拉金普尔医学院附属医院就诊的1,544名患者纳入本院内横断面研究。纳入标准为体温≥37.5°C且伴或不伴皮疹。采用酶联免疫吸附试验(ELISA)和快速检测试剂盒(RDT)对麻疹、风疹、登革热、水痘-带状疱疹、基孔肯雅病毒、日本脑炎(JE)、恙虫病东方体、钩端螺旋体及肝炎病毒进行血清学检测。数据分析采用描述性与推断性方法。P值<0.05为差异有统计学意义。结果:1,544例(100%)患者均有发热,其次为头痛856例(55.44%)、咳嗽636例(41.19%)、呕吐476例(30.83%)、腹痛347例(22.47%)、痢疾59例(3.82%)、腹泻52例(3.37%)、意识不清46例(2.98%),21例(1.36%)出现皮疹。发热与头痛合并发生856例(55.44%)、与咳嗽合并发生636例(41.19%)、与全身疼痛合并发生481例(31.15%)、与呕吐合并发生476例(30.83%)。研究发现感染率存在季节性变化,高峰出现在雨季。确诊病例中,恙虫病133/817例(16.28%)为最常见,其次为钩端螺旋体病129/473例(27.27%)、登革热84/1,273例(6.59%)、日本脑炎20/87例(22.99%),部分患者存在混合感染。结论:本研究强调综合临床与实验室方法在急性发热疾病诊断中的重要性。恙虫病、钩端螺旋体病及登革热被确定为主要病因,凸显加强 监测 与诊断能力的必要性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 急性发热疾病(AFI)包括一系列以发热为特征的疾病,通常由多种病原体引起。病原体的多样性给诊断和治疗带来了挑战,尤其是在诊断资源有限的地区。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项基于医院的横断面研究,于2024年1月至12月期间在印度阿萨姆邦北拉基姆普尔的拉基姆普尔医学系和医院进行,共纳入1,544名患者。所有发热(≥37.5°C)伴有或不伴有皮疹的患者均被纳入研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 对麻疹、风疹、登革热、水痘-带状疱疹病毒、基孔肯雅病毒、日本脑炎(JE)、恙虫病东方体、钩端螺旋体和肝炎病毒进行了血清学检测,使用酶联免疫吸附测定(ELISA)和快速检测测试(RDT)试剂盒。数据采用描述性与推断性统计方法进行分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究发现感染率存在季节性变化,高峰出现在季风月份。多数阳性病例归因于:丛林斑疹伤寒 133/817(16.28%)、钩端螺旋体病 129/473(27.27%)、登革热 84/1273(6.59%)及日本脑炎 20/87(22.99%),部分病例为混合感染。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究强调了在诊断AFI时整合临床与实验室方法的重要性。恙虫病、钩端螺旋体病和登革热被确定为主要病因,突显了提升监测和诊断能力的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果突显了在资源有限地区改善诊断工具和监测系统的必要性,以应对AFI的多样化病原体。感染率的季节性变化可为暴发预测和资源分配提供公共卫生策略依据。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于横断面设计,无法建立因果关系或时间关系。由于基于单一医院的数据,且未考虑更广泛的人群趋势,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Innovative Diseases of Infection and Changes in the Climate
papers.abstract: Emerging infectious diseases (EIDs) are on the move, and with climate change.Climate change is influencing the global spread of EIDs. Climate change is impacting the ecological cycles of diseases, vectors, and hosts because of increasing temperatures, changes in rainfall and increased frequency of extreme weather events. This narrative review briefly summarizes the research conducted on climate-sensitive infectious diseases and the main mechanisms through which these changes are thought to occur. Drought, flood and infrastructure failures are increasingly associated with food- and water-borne diseases (FWBD), such as cholera and leptospirosis. Vector-borne diseases that are spreading to temperate and highland areas include dengue, chikungunya, malaria, and Lyme disease. More zoonotic spillovers (such as Ebola, Nipah and SARS-CoV-2) are observed in the environment where there are changes. This covers new challenges such as microorganisms from perma frost and thermotolerant infections of fungus. Instead of offering new epidemiological modeling, this review makes use of current estimates of the Global Burden of Disease (GBD). According to the estimations, the burden of infectious diseases is expected to rise in susceptible regions affected by climate change, such as South Asia, Latin America, and sub-Saharan Africa. Inadequate monitoring systems, health inequities brought on by climate change, and disrupted data sources are some of the biggest gaps in response.Pathogen genome advancements, satellite surveillance, AI-based forecasting, and One Health approaches provide useful ways to stop issues before they start. Creating transdisciplinary, egalitarian, and climate-responsive public health systems is essential to reducing the rising risks of infectious illnesses connected with climate change. Further research on infectious diseases and climate change should concentrate on non-vector-borne, direct-transmission pathogens and expand research in tropical areas. In low- and middle-income countries, local research was usually ignored. The dearth of thorough, socially inclusive, and regionally balanced research on infectious diseases has hindered our comprehension of the true effects of climate change on health.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the impact of climate change on dengue virus and dengue disease, including how climate factors influence the spread of the virus and the emergence of new challenges related to its transmission and effects.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature on climate-sensitive infectious diseases, utilizing current estimates from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) without introducing new epidemiological modeling. It includes general observations about climate change's influence on disease ecology and vectors.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that climate change is affecting the ecological cycles of diseases, vectors, and hosts, particularly through rising temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, and extreme weather events. It also notes that the burden of infectious diseases, including dengue, is expected to increase in vulnerable regions such as South Asia, Latin America, and sub-Saharan Africa.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies gaps in monitoring systems, health inequities, and disrupted data sources as major challenges in responding to climate-related infectious diseases. It also points out the lack of thorough, socially inclusive, and regionally balanced research, especially in low- and middle-income countries.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on non-vector-borne, direct-transmission pathogens and expand studies in tropical areas. It also emphasizes the importance of integrating pathogen genome advancements, satellite surveillance, AI-based forecasting, and One Health approaches to address these challenges effectively.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the relationship between climate change and dengue virus, emphasizing how rising temperatures, changes in rainfall, and extreme weather events are altering the ecological cycles of the virus and its vectors. It highlights the increasing burden of dengue in vulnerable regions and the need for improved monitoring systems and data sources. The review also calls for more research on non-vector-borne pathogens and the integration of advanced technologies like AI and satellite surveillance to enhance preparedness. Despite the lack of new epidemiological modeling, it underscores the importance of addressing health inequities and strengthening public health systems to mitigate the risks posed by climate-sensitive infectious diseases.

papers.abstract_zh: 新发感染性疾病(EIDs)正在全球范围内扩散,而气候变化正在加速这一进程。气候变化正在影响疾病的生态循环、媒介和宿主,主要通过气温上升、降水模式改变以及极端天气事件频率增加所致。本叙事综述简要总结了针对气候敏感性传染病的研究及其主要作用机制。干旱、洪水和基础设施故障与食源性及水源性疾病(如霍乱和钩端螺旋体病)的关联日益密切。由媒介传播的疾病正在向温带和高原地区扩散,包括登革热、基孔肯雅热、疟疾和莱姆病。在环境变化的背景下,更多的人兽共患跨物种溢出(如埃博拉病毒、尼帕病毒和SARS-CoV-2)被观察到。这还涉及新的挑战,如永久冻土层中微生物的释放以及嗜热真菌感染。本综述未提供新的流行病学模型,而是利用了《全球疾病负担》(GBD)的当前估计值。根据估计,气候变化影响下的脆弱地区(如南亚、拉丁美洲和撒哈拉以南非洲)的传染病负担预计将上升。监测系统不足、气候变化引发的健康不平等以及数据源中断是应对工作面临的最大缺口。病原体基因组进展、卫星监测、基于人工智能的预测以及‘一个健康’方法为提前防控提供了有效途径。构建跨学科、平等且对气候变化有响应的公共卫生系统,对于降低与气候变化相关的传染病风险至关重要。未来针对传染病与气候变化的研究应侧重于非媒介传播的、直接传播的病原体,并扩大在热带地区的研究。在低收入和中等收入国家,当地研究通常被忽视。缺乏全面、社会包容且区域均衡的传染病研究,阻碍了我们对气候变化对健康真实影响的理解。

papers.title: Deep Learning Classification and Motion-Based Analysis of Aedes aegypti Red-Eye GSS Larvae for SIT Applications.
papers.abstract: Aedes aegypti is a major vector of arboviral diseases, including dengue, Zika, and chikungunya, posing significant global public health challenges. Effective control strategies, such as the sterile insect technique (SIT), require an accurate and reliable sex sorting system to ensure male only releases. Here, we present a compact deep-learning framework for image-based classification of sex-linked eye-color phenotypes and instar stages of Aedes aegypti larvae, complemented by an independent optical flow analysis of larval locomotor behavior. Video recordings of individual larvae were used to generate annotated datasets for training a convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify four experimental groups. In parallel, dense optical flow analysis quantified larval locomotor activity, producing interpretable kinematic descriptors. The classifier reliably distinguished between all groups across validation and test sets, with inference suitable for real-time deployment on low-power hardware. Motion analysis revealed systematic differences: L4 larvae exhibited higher activity than L3, and red-eye individuals showed slightly elevated movement relative to black-eye counterparts, indicating that developmental stage is the primary determinant of motility, with pigmentation exerting a secondary influence. The proposed framework provides accurate image-based classification while independently characterizing locomotor behavior, thereby improving the biological interpretation of the analyzed groups. The image-based classifier offers a practical tool for automated larval sorting in SIT programs, whereas the independent motion-analysis module provides quantitative behavioral descriptors that may support future studies of mosquito biology and vector-control applications.

papers.abstract_zh: 埃及伊蚊是登革热、寨卡病毒病和基孔肯雅热等虫媒病毒病的主要媒介,给全球公共卫生带来重大挑战。有效的控制策略(如不育昆虫技术,SIT)需要准确可靠的性别分选系统,以确保仅释放雄性个体。本研究提出了一种紧凑的深度学习框架,用于基于图像的埃及伊蚊幼虫性连锁眼色表型与龄期分类,并辅以独立的光流分析对幼虫运动行为进行量化。通过对单个幼虫的视频录像生成标注数据集,训练卷积神经网络(CNN)以分类四个实验组。同时,密集光流分析量化幼虫运动活性,生成可解释的运动学描述符。分类器在验证集和测试集上可靠区分所有实验组,且推理适用于低功耗硬件的实时部署。运动分析显示系统性差异:L4幼虫的活动性高于L3幼虫,红眼个体较黑眼个体表现出略高的运动活性,表明发育阶段是运动性的主要决定因素,而色素沉着发挥次要影响。所提框架在实现准确图像分类的同时,独立表征运动行为,从而提升所分析群体的生物学解释力。基于图像的分类器为SIT项目中的自动化幼虫分选提供了实用工具,而独立的运动分析模块则提供了定量行为描述符,可能支持未来蚊虫生物学与虫媒病毒病控制应用的研究。

papers.title: Analysis of Count Time Series Through Integer‐Valued Autoregressive (INAR) Process With Zero‐Inflation and Seasonality
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In this article, we study a count time‐series data of weekly dengue cases in Kaohsiung City, Taiwan during the period 2009–2012, where the problems of a large number of zeros or zero‐inflation and seasonality arise together. To capture both features, we consider an application‐oriented zero‐inflated seasonal PINAR framework based on zero‐inflated Poisson innovations. We also incorporate an exogenous variable, namely the weekly maximum temperature, in the innovations to study the effect of temperature on the number of dengue cases as many studies have found that temperature is a significant factor in spreading dengue infections globally. The proposed model can capture both the non‐recovery cases from the previous time point and the new cases coming at the current time point. The distributional and forecasting properties of the proposed model are derived. The consistency and asymptotic normality of the CLS estimator are established under suitable regularity conditions, and simulation experiments are used to examine the finite‐sample estimation and forecasting performance of the proposed model. The proposed model is compared with some existing INAR models. Finally, we analyze the data of weekly dengue cases in Kaohsiung for practical illustration.

The study highlights the importance of addressing zero-inflation and seasonality in dengue surveillance and forecasting. However, the evidence is limited to abstract-level descriptions, and the results are not fully detailed, which affects the strength of the findings. The proposed model offers a novel approach for analyzing dengue time series data, potentially improving public health strategies for outbreak prediction and management.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenges of analyzing count time series data with zero-inflation and seasonality, specifically in the context of dengue cases in Kaohsiung City, Taiwan.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed weekly dengue case data from Kaohsiung City, Taiwan, between 2009 and 2012, focusing on the presence of zero-inflation and seasonality in the count time series.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers developed a zero-inflated seasonal PINAR model using weekly maximum temperature as an exogenous variable to study its effect on dengue case numbers.
analysis_en.main_results: The proposed model was compared with existing INAR models to evaluate its performance in capturing zero-inflation and seasonality in dengue case data.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The model's ability to account for both zero-inflation and seasonality represents a novel approach to analyzing dengue case time series data.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a methodological tool for better understanding and forecasting dengue outbreaks, which can inform public health strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence and does not include detailed statistical results or real-world validation, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

papers.title_zh: 通过整数值自回归(INAR)过程分析零膨胀与季节性计数时间序列:以高雄市登革热病例为例
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT In this article, we study a count time‐series data of weekly dengue cases in Kaohsiung City, Taiwan during the period 2009–2012, where the problems of a large number of zeros or zero‐inflation and seasonality arise together. To capture both features, we consider an application‐oriented zero‐inflated seasonal PINAR framework based on zero‐inflated Poisson innovations. We also incorporate an exogenous variable, namely the weekly maximum temperature, in the innovations to study the effect of temperature on the number of dengue cases as many studies have found that temperature is a significant factor in spreading dengue infections globally. The proposed model can capture both the non‐recovery cases from the previous time point and the new cases coming at the current time point. The distributional and forecasting properties of the proposed model are derived. The consistency and asymptotic normality of the CLS estimator are established under suitable regularity conditions, and simulation experiments are used to examine the finite‐sample estimation and forecasting performance of the proposed model. The proposed model is compared with some existing INAR models. Finally, we analyze the data of weekly dengue cases in Kaohsiung for practical illustration.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 本文研究了台湾高雄市2009—2012年期间每周登革热病例的计数时间序列数据,该数据同时存在大量零值(零膨胀)与季节性问题。为同时捕捉这两个特征,我们考虑了一种面向应用的零膨胀季节性PINAR框架,该框架基于零膨胀泊松创新。我们还在创新项中纳入一个外生变量,即每周最高气温,以研究气温对登革热病例数量的影响,因为多项研究已发现气温是全球登革热传播的重要因素。所提模型可同时捕捉前一时间点未恢复的病例与当前时间点新增的病例。本文推导了所提模型的分布性质与预测性质。在适当的正则性条件下,我们证明了CLS估计量的一致性与渐近正态性,并通过模拟实验检验了所提模型在有限样本估计与预测性能。最后,我们将所提模型与若干现有INAR模型进行比较,并以高雄市每周登革热病例数据为例进行实证分析。

papers.title: Chikungunya-Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Rare Fatal Case
papers.abstract: Chikungunya fever is an arboviral disease caused by an alphavirus belonging to the family Togaviridae. It commonly presents with fever, severe arthralgia, rash, and myalgia, while severe pulmonary involvement causing acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is rare. We report a 62-year-old man with obesity, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnoea, coronary artery disease, and interstitial lung disease, who presented with high-grade fever, severe arthralgia, facial puffiness, and rapidly progressive dyspnoea, following recent travel to Lucknow, India. On admission, he had severe hypoxemia with a PaO2/FiO2 ratio below 100, requiring mechanical ventilation. During intubation, he developed cardiac arrest but achieved return of spontaneous circulation after cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Chikungunya IgM and reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) were positive. Chest imaging showed diffuse bilateral infiltrates and ground-glass opacities consistent with severe ARDS. Dengue, malaria, and scrub typhus were excluded. The patient was managed with lung-protective ventilation, prone positioning, and corticosteroids according to the Meduri protocol with transient improvement. However, he later developed worsening respiratory failure and multiorgan dysfunction and eventually succumbed after 41 days of hospitalization. Although chikungunya is not typically considered a respiratory virus, clinicians should recognize that severe pulmonary manifestations, including ARDS, may occur, particularly in elderly patients with significant comorbidities.

papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya fever is an arboviral disease caused by an alphavirus belonging to the family Togaviridae. It commonly presents with fever, severe arthralgia, rash, and myalgia, while severe pulmonary involvement causing acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is rare. We report a 62-year-old man with obesity, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnoea, coronary artery disease, and interstitial lung disease, who presented with high-grade fever, severe arthralgia, facial puffiness, and rapidly progressive dyspnoea, following recent travel to Lucknow, India. On admission, he had severe hypoxemia with a PaO2/FiO2 ratio below 100, requiring mechanical ventilation. During intubation, he developed cardiac arrest but achieved return of spontaneous circulation after cardiopulmonary resuscitation. The patient was managed with lung-protective ventilation, prone positioning, and corticosteroids according to the Meduri protocol with transient improvement. However, he later developed worsening respiratory failure and multiorgan dysfunction and eventually succumbed after 41 days of hospitalization. Although chikungunya is not typically considered a respiratory virus, clinicians should recognize that severe pulmonary manifestations, including ARDS, may occur, particularly in elderly patients with significant comorbidities.

papers.title: Climate Change and Arboviral Diseases: Challenges for Surveillance and Primary Health Care
papers.abstract: Climate change has emerged as one of the greatest public health challenges of the twenty-first century, profoundly influencing the epidemiology of infectious diseases worldwide. Among the health conditions most directly affected by environmental transformations are arboviral diseases, including dengue, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever, whose transmission dynamics are highly sensitive to variations in temperature, rainfall, humidity, urbanization, and ecosystem disruption. These climatic and environmental changes have expanded the geographic distribution of mosquito vectors, prolonged transmission seasons, and increased the frequency and intensity of outbreaks in tropical and subtropical regions. In countries such as Brazil, where arboviruses already represent a significant public health burden, climate change has intensified existing vulnerabilities and imposed new demands on health systems, particularly regarding disease surveillance, prevention, and healthcare delivery. This academic essay critically examines the relationship between climate change and the growing burden of arboviral diseases, emphasizing the challenges faced by epidemiological surveillance systems and Primary Health Care (PHC). The discussion explores the ecological mechanisms linking climate variability to vector proliferation, the organizational implications for health services, the importance of integrated surveillance, and the strategic role of PHC in prevention, early diagnosis, community engagement, and intersectoral action. The essay argues that strengthening climate-sensitive health governance and resilient primary healthcare systems is essential for reducing the health impacts of climate-driven arboviral transmission and protecting vulnerable populations.

elements_zh.main_results: 这些气候与环境变化已扩大蚊媒媒介的地理分布,延长传播季节,并增加热带与亚热带地区暴发的频率与强度。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,亟需加强气候敏感型卫生治理与韧性基层卫生保健系统,以减轻气候驱动的虫媒病毒性传播的健康影响,并保护脆弱人群。

papers.abstract_zh: 气候变化已成为21世纪最严峻的公共卫生挑战之一,深刻影响着全球传染病的流行病学。在直接受环境变化影响的健康问题中,虫媒病毒性疾病(包括登革热、寨卡病毒病、基孔肯雅热与黄热病)的传播动态对温度、降水、湿度、城市化及生态系统破坏等变化高度敏感。这些气候与环境变化已扩大蚊媒媒介的地理分布,延长传播季节,并增加热带与亚热带地区暴发的频率与强度。在巴西等虫媒病毒已构成显著公共卫生负担的国家,气候变化加剧了既有脆弱性,并为卫生系统带来新的需求,特别是在疾病监测、预防与医疗服务提供方面。本学术论文对气候变化与虫媒病毒性疾病负担日益加重之间的关系进行了批判性审视,强调流行病学监测系统与基层卫生保健(PHC)所面临的挑战。讨论涵盖了气候变异与媒介增殖的生态机制、卫生服务的组织层面影响、综合监测的重要性,以及PHC在预防、早期诊断、社区参与与跨部门行动中的战略作用。论文认为,加强气候敏感型卫生治理与韧性基层卫生保健系统,对于减轻气候驱动的虫媒病毒性传播的健康影响并保护脆弱人群至关重要。

analysis_zh.main_results: 这些气候与环境变化已扩大蚊媒媒介的地理分布,延长传播季节,并增加热带与亚热带地区暴发的频率与强度。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,气候变化加剧了既有脆弱性,并为卫生系统带来新的需求,特别是在疾病监测、预防与医疗服务提供方面。论文强调了综合监测的必要性,以及PHC在应对此类挑战中的战略作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,亟需加强气候敏感型卫生治理与韧性基层卫生保健系统,以减轻气候驱动的虫媒病毒性传播的健康影响,并保护脆弱人群。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告具体局限性或证据强度评估。本论文基于一般性观察与启示,证据强度被认为属于中等水平。

Search|t Updates Countries Disasters Organizations Topics Jobs Training Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA Vanuatu Vanuatu Dengue Outbreak Situation Report #10 (South-West Efate, Shefa Province) Format Situation Report Source SPC Posted 21 Aug 2026 Originally published 21 Aug 2026 Attachments Download Report (PDF | 363.26 KB) Key updates: A total of 91 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases have been reported since the start of the outbreak, including 15 new cases in EW33, representing the highest weekly case count to date. The outbreak remains active with ongoing community transmission across South-West Efate. Dengue Virus Type 1 (DENV-1) has been confirmed as the circulating serotype. 14 dengue-related hospitalisations have been reported; all patients have recovered and been discharged. No severe dengue cases or deaths have been recorded. Cases continue to be reported across multiple areas of Efate Island, with the highest proportions from Erakor, Port Vila, Eratap, and Pango. analysis.time: The report was published on 21 August 2026. The outbreak has been ongoing, with the highest weekly case count recorded as of this report.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak is occurring in South-West Efate, Shefa Province, Vanuatu, affecting multiple areas including Erakor, Port Vila, Eratap, and Pango.
analysis.event: A dengue outbreak is ongoing in South-West Efate, Shefa Province, Vanuatu, with laboratory-confirmed cases reported since the start of the outbreak. Dengue Virus Type 1 (DENV-1) has been confirmed as the circulating serotype.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: A total of 91 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases have been reported, with 15 new cases in EW33. No severe dengue cases or deaths have been recorded. 14 hospitalisations have been reported, but all patients have recovered.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The outbreak remains active with ongoing community transmission. The situation report indicates that the outbreak is being monitored, and no severe cases or deaths have been recorded. The report is a partial summary, and the full original article body could not be extracted.

analysis.brief_en: Vanuatu's dengue outbreak, currently active in South-West Efate, Shefa Province, has reported 91 laboratory-confirmed cases since its start, including 15 new cases in EW33, the highest weekly count to date. Dengue Virus Type 1 (DENV-1) is the circulating serotype. No severe dengue cases or deaths have been recorded, and 14 dengue-related hospitalisations have been reported, with all patients recovering and discharged. The outbreak is ongoing with community transmission across multiple areas of Efate Island, such as Erakor, Port Vila, Eratap, and Pango. The report, published on 21 August 2026, is a partial summary, and the full original article body could not be extracted. The situation remains under monitoring, with no indication of severe health-system effects reported.

No severe dengue cases or deaths have been recorded, and 14 dengue-related hospitalisations have been reported, with all patients recovering and discharged. The outbreak is ongoing with community transmission across multiple areas of Efate Island, such as Erakor, Port Vila, Eratap, and Pango. The report, published on 21 August 2026, is a partial summary, and the full original article body could not be extracted. The situation remains under monitoring, with no indication of severe health-system effects reported.
